case_name: K. S. Paripoornan and Others v State of Kerala and Others
facts: The notification u/s. 3(1) of the Kerala Land Acquisition Act was issued on March 21, 1978.
Declaration u/s. 6 was made on May 15, 1979.
The Land Acquisition Officer (Collector) passed the award on December 30, 1980 and possession of acquired lands taken some time in 1981.
The claimants were not satisfied with the award. They asked for a reference u/s. 18 which was made.
The civil court gave its decision on February 28, 1985, enhancing the compensation.
The Land Acquisition Amendment Bill, which was later enacted into Amendment Act 68 of 1984, was introduced in Parliament on April 30, 1982.

The award of the Collector in this case was made on December 30, 1980, i.e., prior to April 30, 1982 and the decision of the civil court on reference u/s. 18 is dated February 28, 1985, i.e., subsequent to the coming into force of the Act.
issues: Whether the claimants are entitled to the benefit of S. 23(1-A)?
petitioner_arguments: The learned counsel for the claimants relies upon the aforesaid decision of a three Judge bench of this Court in support of his contention that even in a case like the present one, the said benefit is available.
respondent_arguments: Shri T. S. Krishnamurthy Iyer, the learned counsel for the State of Kerala questions the correctness of this reasoning.
court_reasoning: The view expressed by the bench does not appear to be in accordance with the language and intention of the Amendment Act.
S. 23(1) enjoins the Court to take into consideration six factors, as enumerated therein, in determining the amount of compensation to be awarded for the land acquired under the Act.
holding: The view taken by a three Judge bench of this Court in Union of India v. Zora Singh (1991 Indlaw SC 383) required reconsideration.
The benefit of sub-section (1-A) of s. 23 is not available to the claimants here.
cases_cited: K. S. Paripoornan and Others v State of Kerala
